elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Latin & Greek Suffix Stress Rules (-ian, -ious, -ial, -graphy, -logy)
1. Definition: Academic vocabulary borrowed from Latin and Greek follows rigid suffix-driven primary stress assignment.

2. Rule: 1. -ian, -ious, -ial, -ic, -ical = Primary stress on syllable IMMEDIATELY BEFORE suffix (muSIcian, cuRIous, ofFIcial, fanTAStic). 2. -graphy, -logy, -meter, -metry = Primary stress on 3rd syllable from end (phoTOGraphy, biOLogy, therMOMeter).
3. Why? Latin stress rules (penultimate/antepenultimate rule) were fossilized when suffixes were adopted into English.
4. How to recognize? Identify Latinate/Greek suffixes in academic words.
5. Common examples: musician /mjuːˈzɪʃən/, curious /ˈkjʊəriəs/, official /əˈfɪʃəl/, photography /fəˈtɒgrəfi/, biology /baɪˈɒlədʒi/, thermometer /θərˈmɒmɪtər/
6. Counter-examples: Germanic suffixes (-ness, -ful, -less) which NEVER shift stress.
7. Exceptions: politic /ˈpɒlɪtɪk/ -> political /pəˈlɪtɪkəl/ (stress remains on same syllable).
8. Common mistakes: Keeping stress on root when adding Greek suffix (*PHOto-graphy instead of pho-TOG-raphy).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: -ian/-ious/-ial = Stress JUST BEFORE suffix! -graphy/-logy = Count 3 from end!
10. Key vocabulary: Latinate suffix, Greek suffix, antepenultimate stress, stress shift, academic lexicon
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🔵 B2
13. Associated Visual: 🎓 Academic mortarboard over suffix stress formulas.
14. Key Takeaway: -ic/-tion/-ian = Syllable BEFORE! -graphy/-logy = 3rd from end!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Where is stress in 'photo' vs 'photography'? (PHOto = 1st syllable; phoTOGraphy = 2nd syllable / 3rd from end)
CCQ 2: Where does stress fall for suffixes like '-ian', '-ious', '-ial'? (On the syllable immediately before the suffix)
CCQ 3: How many syllables from the end is stress placed for '-logy' in 'biology'? (3rd syllable from the end)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
